streams.opening: Reviewers wrote on GitLab MR !#, which the user authored and is reworking. Prepare each topic below in the background, so its card carries your proposal by the time the user opens it. Nobody reads your replies: only what you store counts. Run every command as `cd {SRC}/agent-skills-demo-scroll && python# {HOME}/.claude/skills/rework-mr/scripts/threads.py <command> --iid #`. Spell that out in full in every call: zsh, the shell here, runs no command kept in a variable. Pass every text in single quotes, an apostrophe in it as `'\''`: inside double quotes the shell runs whatever is in backticks. Store with `propose` (or `keep-plan`, below) and nothing else: never edit code, commit, push, post, resolve, or show anything (no `set`, `agree`, `post`, `open`, `later`, `quote --focus`, `show_topic`). Read first: `bodies` (every open thread, first and last comment), then `quote <t>` for each topic (the code the comment is on and the whole thread), then the code itself where the point needs it. For each, store one proposal: `propose <t> --says needs|fyi --why '<#–# English sentences: what the reviewer asks, what the code does, and the trade-off; end on a **Recommendation:** sentence>' [--outcome fix|reply|push-back|question --plan '<one sentence: what to do>'] [--answer-now] [--change - <<'CHANGE_EOF' … CHANGE_EOF]`. `fyi` where the comment asks nothing of the user (a thank-you, an OK on what they did): no outcome then. `needs` takes `--outcome` and `--plan`; `fix` for every plan that changes code, a push-back that also adds a comment included, the others for a plan that only replies. For a small fix add `--change -` with the change on stdin as `@@ <path>:<first>-<last>` blocks, each followed by the new lines that replace those lines (the diff is built from the file; never write one by hand): the idea and its main change at its origin (the rename where the name is defined, the new parameter in the signature), never the call sites it adapts. `--answer-now` on a fix whose plan answers the reviewer ahead of it: they asked a question, or offered options and the plan picks one. In `--why` and `--plan` alike, every identifier, path and value in backticks: the card draws them as code. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. - t#: Miriam opened it. input.message:
I stored proposals for all 12 topics, t2 to t13: 3 fixes, 5 replies, 2 push-backs, 2 questions and 1 fyi.

**Fixes, each with a one-line change:**
- **t2:** reword the `Link` comment to say it returns a react-router `RouterLink`.
- **t4:** rewrite the `Spinner` comment to list its `size` and `variant` props. The current comment also says "three sizes" when there are four (`sm` to `xl`), and the rewrite fixes that.
- **t12:** the login function uses no hook; the `useLogin` hook in `src/lib/auth.tsx` calls it. The comment now says it is "used by `useLogin` in `@/lib/auth`".

**Replies:**
- **t3:** the `MDPreview` comment is still accurate; it still sanitizes the parsed markdown.
- **t7:** the `InputField` comment is about the form binding, so it holds on mobile too.
- **t8:** the code spells "sanitize" the US way everywhere and "sanitised" appears nowhere. The `SelectField` comment has neither word.
- **t13:** neither `README.md` nor `docs/` mentions feature flags, so `src/config/feature-flags.ts` stays the only source.

**Push-backs:**
- **t10:** the app is a Vite single-page app with no server rendering, so marking only `ContentLayout` client-only would mislead.
- **t11:** keep the `Notification` comment. It separates one toast from the `Notifications` list, and every shared component in this MR has one.

**Questions:**
- **t6:** the `FieldWrapper` comment already starts with "A". The reply asks whether she meant `Head.tsx`, which does start with "The".
- **t9:** nothing under `docs/` covers `Head`. The reply asks which design doc she means.

**FYI:**
- **t5:** the `Table` comment is 47 columns, already under 80.

Stored: 12 proposals (t2 to t13).
